question:
package main
func main() {
  ch := make(chan int)
  ch <- 1
  v := <-ch
  println(v)
}
explanation: Unbuffered channels block on send until a receiver is ready; main thread sends before spawning a goroutine to receive, causing deadlock.

question:
package main
func main() {
  ch := make(chan int, 1)
  ch <- 1
  ch <- 2
  println(<-ch)
}
explanation: Buffered channel capacity is 1; two sends without receives cause the second send to block, deadlocking since no goroutine waits.
Range over a closed buffered channel drains remaining values (1, 2) then exits; close is safe after sends complete.

question:
package main
func main() {
  ch := make(chan int)
  close(ch)
  v, ok := <-ch
  println(v, ok)
}
explanation: Receiving from a closed channel returns zero value and ok=false, allowing cleanup code without panic.

question:
package main
func main() {
  ch := make(chan int)
  v := <-ch
  close(ch)
  println(v)
}
explanation: Receive on unbuffered channel blocks waiting for a send; when nothing sends, deadlock occurs, and Go panics on goroutine exit.

question:
package main
func main() {
  ch := make(chan int, 5)
  ch <- 1
  ch <- 2
  ch <- 3
  len := len(ch)
  cap := cap(ch)
  println(len, cap)
}
explanation: len(ch) returns buffered items count (3), cap(ch) returns channel capacity (5); buffered channel shows both.
Directional channels (send-only, receive-only) enforce one-way communication; sender goroutine sends, receiver goroutine receives synchronously.
Select picks a ready channel; ch1 blocks (no sender), but ch2 has buffered 42, so select receives from ch2.
Sending on a closed channel panics; close marks channel as finished and forbids further sends.
Select with default executes default when channel full; buffered channel capacity 3 accepts 0-2, then default catches 3-4.
